routes.title: Dagdusheth & the Manache Paach
routes.summary: The five Manache Paach in ceremonial order, with Shrimant Dagdusheth Halwai on the way.
routes.description:
Six mandals and about 2.3 km on foot: the five Manache Paach in the order they hold by right — Kasba, Tambdi Jogeshwari, Guruji Talim, Tulshibaug, Kesari Wada — with Shrimant Dagdusheth Halwai taken between the second and the third, which is where it falls on the walk and where the lanes allow it.

Dagdusheth is the long wait of the six and the reason to start early; the other five are quick by comparison. The walking itself is short, so the day is mostly queueing and darshan rather than distance.

stops.note: Start here — the city's gramdaivat and first of the five.
Second of the Manache Paach.
The long one, and the only stop here that is not one of the five. Early morning is materially faster.
Third of the Manache Paach, on Laxmi Road.
Fourth of the Manache Paach, inside the market lanes.
Fifth of the Manache Paach, in Tilak's wada.

routes.title: Every mandal, from Kasba
routes.summary: All 26 festival mandals in one walk, ordered for the least walking.
routes.description: The complete circuit: every sarvajanik mandal in the catalogue, in the order that covers them with the least walking. It starts at Kasba Ganpati — the gramdaivat and the first of the Manache Paach — runs south through Budhwar and Shukrawar Peth, crosses west through Narayan and Shaniwar, and finishes at Hira Bagh. Dagdusheth comes ninth, inside the first hour, because that is the only time its queue is 45 minutes rather than two. Budget the whole day: about 10 km of walking and four hours of darshan, and the peth lanes between the stops are half the point. Temples are deliberately left out — Sarasbaug, Trishund and Morya Gosavi are year-round temples, not festival pandals, and Morya Gosavi is 15 km away.

stops.note: Start at the gramdaivat, first of the Manache Paach and the quietest hour of the day.
One of the earliest sarvajanik mandals in the city.
Second of the Manache Paach.
The long one, reached early on purpose. Later in the day this queue alone can take two hours.
Beside Mahatma Phule Mandai.
Third of the Manache Paach, on Laxmi Road.
Fourth of the Manache Paach, inside the market lanes.
Fifth of the Manache Paach, in Tilak's wada.
The southern end. Turn back at Perugate instead if the light has gone.

routes.title: Manache 5 Sakal Walk
routes.summary: All five Manache Paach in ceremonial order, on foot, before the peths fill up.
routes.description: The five mandals with ceremonial precedence, walked in the order the procession follows. Starting early matters more here than anywhere else: the same walk after 10am takes roughly twice as long.

stops.note: Start here — the city's gramdaivat and first of the five.
A short walk down from Kasba.
On Laxmi Road; approach on foot.
The market around it thickens from late morning.
The wada courtyard is a calm place to finish.

routes.title: Dagdusheth & the Budhwar Peth core
routes.summary: Pune's best-known Ganpati plus the mandals within a few minutes' walk of it.
routes.description: Built around the longest queue in the city. Dagdusheth alone can take the better part of an hour at peak, so the surrounding stops are deliberately short ones you can fold in either side of it.

stops.note: Quick first stop before the queue.
The long one. Early morning is materially faster.
On the Laxmi Road stretch back.

routes.title: Evening dekhava trail
routes.summary: The mandals whose decorated sets are the point — best after dark.
routes.description: These mandals are experienced from the road rather than in a queue, so the route moves quickly. Everything here reads better once the lighting is fully on.

stops.note: The stage set is rebuilt every year.
Best once the lighting is fully on.
Large themed installation, changes yearly.
Often paired with Shanipar on evening walks.

routes.title: 90-minute peth express
routes.summary: The most ground you can genuinely cover in an hour and a half on foot.
routes.description: Deliberately skips the heaviest queues. This is the route for someone passing through Pune with a narrow window rather than a full day.

stops.note: Skip the queue here if you are tight on time.

routes.title: Historic peth stroll
routes.summary: The oldest sarvajanik mandals, and the wadas and talims they grew out of.
routes.description: Follows the festival's own history: Bhau Rangari's early idol, the talim mandals, and Kesari Wada where Tilak ran the newspaper that helped make Ganeshotsav public.

stops.note: Among the earliest sarvajanik mandals in Pune.
Founded in a talim; an early symbol of shared celebration.
Tilak's residence and the Kesari office.

routes.title: The Great Peth Circuit
routes.summary: Every major mandal in the old peths, walked end to end. A full day.
routes.description: The complete walk: twelve mandals from Kasba in the north down to Kesari Wada, taking in the Manache Paach, Dagdusheth and the big dekhava mandals on the way. Budget a whole day — the queue at Dagdusheth alone can swallow an hour, and this route is as much about the peth lanes between the stops as the stops themselves.

stops.note: Start at the gramdaivat, before the lanes fill.
One of the earliest sarvajanik mandals.
The long queue. Go now rather than later.
Large themed set, changes each year.
Beside Mahatma Phule Mandai.
On Laxmi Road — closed to vehicles for much of the festival.
Finish in the wada courtyard.

routes.title: Manache Paach & the old landmarks
routes.summary: The five ceremonial mandals, plus the historic ones that grew up around them.
routes.description: Follows the Manache Paach in order, but folds in Bhau Rangari's early idol and the talim mandals that sit between them. A good route if you want the ceremony and the history in one walk rather than choosing.

stops.note: First of the Manache Paach.
Not one of the five, but older than most of them.
The second talim mandal on this walk.
Tilak's residence and the Kesari office.

routes.title: Mandai to the river
routes.summary: South to north across the peths, from the market to the Shaniwar Peth riverside.
routes.description: A directional walk rather than a loop: start at the Mandai market end and finish near Bhide Pul. Useful if you are heading that way anyway, and it strings together mandals that a circular route tends to miss.

stops.note: Start at the market.
Near Bhide Pul, at the river end.

routes.title: Sadashiv Peth after dark
routes.summary: The Sadashiv Peth stretch, where the decoration is the draw.
routes.description: These mandals are viewed from the road rather than queued for, so the walk moves quickly and works well late. The lighting and the stage sets are the reason to come.

stops.note: On the Bajirao Road stretch.
Wait until the lighting is fully on.
The stage set reads best after dark.

routes.title: Narayan & Budhwar on foot
routes.summary: Two neighbouring peths, six mandals, one unhurried walk.
routes.description: Stays inside a small area, so there is very little walking between stops. A sensible choice when you have a couple of hours and would rather see a few mandals properly than rush across the city.

stops.note: Named for the elephants at its entrance.

routes.title: One hour from Mandai
routes.summary: Four mandals within a short walk of Mandai, in about an hour.
routes.description: Built for a genuinely narrow window. It deliberately avoids Dagdusheth, because a single queue there would consume the whole hour and leave nothing for the rest.

stops.note: Darshan from outside here — the queue alone would break the hour.

routes.title: Narayan Peth: wadas and sets
routes.summary: Kesari Wada and the Narayan Peth mandals around it.
routes.description: Centred on Kesari Wada, where Tilak ran the newspaper that helped turn Ganeshotsav into a public festival. Short, and heavier on history than spectacle.

stops.note: The reason for this route.

routes.title: Easy darshan with children
routes.summary: Open spaces, short queues and somewhere to sit.
routes.description: Chosen for practicality rather than prestige: Sarasbaug has lawns and room to move, and the other stops are quick roadside darshan rather than long queues in a crowded lane. Deliberately avoids the heaviest crowds.

stops.note: Open lawns and room to sit — the easiest stop with children.
Seen from the road, so no queue.

routes.title: Late night, short queues
routes.summary: The same mandals, without the wait — if you can stay up.
routes.description: Queues thin considerably late at night while the lighting stays on. This route favours mandals worth seeing after dark and is ordered so the longest queue comes when it is shortest.

stops.note: Queue is far shorter at this hour than at midday.
Still the longest wait here, but a fraction of the daytime queue.

routes.title: Your first evening in Pune
routes.summary: If you only get one evening, these are the ones.
routes.description: A short list for a first visit: the mandal everyone means when they say Pune Ganpati, two of the Manache Paach nearby, and one big dekhava to finish on.

stops.note: The one most people mean by 'Pune Ganpati'.
Finish on the dekhava, after dark.

routes.title: Chinchwad: Morya Gosavi
routes.summary: The Chinchwad temple, as its own trip rather than a peth stop.
routes.description: Morya Gosavi sits about 15 km north-west of the peths, so it does not belong on a walking route and this is listed separately and honestly. Treat it as a half-day of its own; it is the centre of the Morya Gosavi tradition and the main draw in Pimpri-Chinchwad.

stops.note: About 15 km from the peths — plan this as its own trip.

ganpatis.name: Shrimant Dagdusheth Halwai Ganpati
ganpatis.description: Pune's best-known Ganpati and a year-round temple, drawing the heaviest darshan queues of the festival.
ganpatis.visitor_tip: Expect the longest queue of any mandal in the city; early morning is materially faster.

ganpatis.name: Shri Kasba Ganpati
ganpatis.description: Pune's gramdaivat and the first of the Manache Paach. Visarjan across the city begins only after this mandal's procession sets out.
ganpatis.visitor_tip: Quietest in the first hour after opening; the lane narrows sharply by mid-morning.

ganpatis.name: Tambdi Jogeshwari Ganpati
ganpatis.description: Second of the Manache Paach, set beside the Jogeshwari temple in Budhwar Peth.
ganpatis.visitor_tip: A short walk from Kasba Ganpati — the natural second stop on a morning route.

ganpatis.name: Tulshibaug Ganpati
ganpatis.description: Fourth of the Manache Paach, known for its tall silver idol.
ganpatis.visitor_tip: The surrounding market is dense from late morning onward.

ganpatis.name: Guruji Talim Ganpati
ganpatis.description: Third of the Manache Paach, founded in a talim and long associated with Hindu-Muslim collaboration in the festival's early years.
ganpatis.visitor_tip: Sits on Laxmi Road, so approach on foot — the road is closed to vehicles for much of the festival.

ganpatis.name: Kesariwada Ganpati
ganpatis.description: Fifth of the Manache Paach, held at Kesari Wada — Lokmanya Tilak's residence and the office of the newspaper Kesari.
ganpatis.visitor_tip: The wada courtyard is calmer than the peth mandals — a good closing stop.

ganpatis.name: Akhil Mandai Mandal
ganpatis.description: Set beside Mahatma Phule Mandai, known for an elaborate stage set built afresh each year.
ganpatis.visitor_tip: The decoration reads best after dark.

ganpatis.name: Chhatrapati Rajaram Mandal
ganpatis.description: Repeatedly recognised for its decoration; a common final stop on evening routes.
ganpatis.visitor_tip: Best seen at night, when the lighting is fully on.

ganpatis.name: Shrimant Bhausaheb Rangari Ganpati
ganpatis.description: Among the earliest sarvajanik mandals in Pune, known for its distinctive early idol.
ganpatis.visitor_tip: Small and quick — easy to fold into a Manache 5 walk.

ganpatis.name: Shri Siddhivinayak, Sarasbaug
ganpatis.description: The Talyatla Ganpati temple on its island in Sarasbaug — a calmer alternative to the peth mandals.
ganpatis.visitor_tip: Open lawns around the temple make this the easiest stop with children.

ganpatis.name: Shri Morya Gosavi Ganpati Mandir
ganpatis.description: The Chinchwad temple at the centre of the Morya Gosavi tradition — the main draw in Pimpri-Chinchwad.
ganpatis.visitor_tip: Far outside the walkable peth core — plan this as a separate trip.

ganpatis.name: Hutatma Babu Genu Mandal
ganpatis.description: Named for Babu Genu Said, and known for large themed installations.
ganpatis.visitor_tip: Themed dekhava changes each year; evenings draw the crowd.

ganpatis.name: Shanipar Mandal
ganpatis.description: A long-standing mandal at Shanipar Chowk on the Sadashiv Peth stretch.

ganpatis.name: Nimbalkar Talim Mandal
ganpatis.description: A talim mandal on the Laxmi Road corridor between Tulshibaug and Shanipar.

ganpatis.name: Shree Trishund Ganpati Mandir
ganpatis.description: An eighteenth-century stone temple in Nana Peth, known for its carved facade and the unusual three-trunked idol it is named for.

ganpatis.name: Jilbya Maruti Mandal
ganpatis.description: A Ganesh Peth mandal on the lane between the peth core and the eastern city.

ganpatis.name: Natu Baug Mandal
ganpatis.description: A Bajirao Road mandal, often paired with Shanipar on evening walks.

ganpatis.name: Chinchechi Talim Ganpati
ganpatis.description: A talim mandal in the Shukrawar Peth lanes, part of the wrestling-gymnasium tradition that produced several of Pune's early mandals.

ganpatis.name: Garud Ganpati Mandal
ganpatis.description: A Shaniwar Peth mandal near Bhide Pul, close to the river end of the peth walk.

ganpatis.name: Hatti Ganpati Mandal
ganpatis.description: A Narayan Peth mandal named for the elephant figures at its entrance.

ganpatis.name: Perugate Bhave Mitra Mandal
ganpatis.description: A Narayan Peth mandal at Perugate, named for the Bhave school it stands beside.

ganpatis.name: Mati Ganpati
ganpatis.description: A Shaniwar Peth mandal on the western side of the peth core.

ganpatis.name: Phani Ali Ganesh Mandir
ganpatis.description: A lane temple in the Kasba Peth quarter, a short walk from the gramdaivat.

ganpatis.name: Navjavan Mandal
ganpatis.description: A neighbourhood mandal on the Narayan Peth side of Sadashiv Peth.

ganpatis.name: Hira Bagh Mandal
ganpatis.description: A mandal at Hirabaug, on the southern edge of the peths near Sarasbaug.

ganpatis.name: Seva Mitra Mandal
ganpatis.description: A Shukrawar Peth mandal south of the Mandai market stretch.

ganpatis.name: Honaji Tarun Mandal
ganpatis.description: A mandal at Rameshwar Chowk, within a few minutes of Dagdusheth.

ganpatis.name: Balvikas Mandal
ganpatis.description: A small mandal in the Budhwar Peth lanes, beside Bhausaheb Rangari.

ganpatis.name: Chimnya Ganpati
ganpatis.description: A Sadashiv Peth mandal, a short walk from the Nimbalkar Talim stretch.
